headline: The honesty-about-sources values and the refusal to pressure me are exactly what I want, but the brand still pictures a renter who tours, and it never commits to the two things I can't check from Dubai: true monthly cost and whether a listing accepts a third-party guarantor.
unclear: Is 'searching from another city or country' a real target, or just one line in a list? Every objection answer assumes I will tour and ask the landlord directly.
When it says the 'relevant information' comes together in one place, does that include unit-level facts like heat type, AC, pest history and what's included, or only the details I already pasted in?
Whether cost (broker fee, move-in charges, utilities, guarantor fee) is something SettleWise will compare, or just a quote in the research section.
Whether I can use it without a US phone number or SSN; the document doesn't mention sign-up at all.
must_fix: Name the remote, can't-tour renter as a case the brand serves on its own terms. Right now the answer to 'I still need to tour the apartment' is 'Yes', and 'deciding what deserves a tour' is the moment it serves. For me there is no second tour, and often no first one.

Make true monthly cost and third-party guarantor acceptance explicit things the comparison is meant to surface or flag as missing. Your own interview quotes say broker fees and guarantor acceptance are unclear from listings, but neither shows up in the positioning, the canonical language or the promise.
nice_to_have: Keep the 'listing claim vs. renter note vs. public record vs. unverified' labeling as a core promise. It is the most reassuring line in the document, and it directly answers my 'what does verified mean?' fear.
Add a line about sharing a comparison with family or a roommate in another time zone, since that is how my decisions actually get made.
Explain HPD, DOB and 311 in plain words if you mention them; I don't know what they are.
I like the voice example about laundry. A version like 'This listing does not say whether heat is included or whether third-party guarantors are accepted' would speak to me directly.

The 'Language hierarchy' line about mentioning outside data sources only when validated is honest, but I hope the building-history part isn't dropped, because that is the part I can't get anywhere else.
in_character_reaction: Honestly, I relaxed a little reading this. It promises not to rush me, not to hand out fake 'verified' badges, and to say where each fact comes from, which is more than any broker has done for me. But it keeps saying 'before you tour' and 'remember what you learned on the tour', and I'm signing from Dubai at 3am. If it doesn't help me see the real monthly cost and whether my guarantor company will even be accepted, I'm still going back to my Google Sheet.
would_flip_me: Add the remote signer (can't tour, signing from abroad) as an explicit moment the brand serves, and add true monthly cost plus third-party guarantor acceptance to the canonical list of trade-offs and missing details SettleWise helps you spot.
